dataset_name: Nepal district names in Nepali (Constitution of Nepal, Schedule 4)
source: Constitution of Nepal, Schedule 4 (Provinces and districts in each province): Nepali text as published by the Supreme Court of Nepal; official English version as published by the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs
license: Government of Nepal legal text; the constitution is a public law document
attribution: Constitution of Nepal 2015 (2072 BS), Schedule 4. Supreme Court of Nepal; Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs.
method: Nepali source PDF SHA-256 32912851de3c214c4aa03e7b4fa57ea5be71d636dc6b7d7fc4d4ba9924dbfe18 (route: direct); its text layer is in the legacy Preeti font and was mapped to Unicode with npttf2utf 0.3.7. English source PDF SHA-256 08088fbdcd3b8d46d02440e0474cdd764983f742e7f07fdb95fd7d43e354fc89 (route: internet-archive, fetched from https://web.archive.org/web/20240616183854id_/https%3A//www.moljpa.gov.np/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Constitution-of-Nepal-2nd-amd.-English.pdf). Both schedules were parsed from pdftotext -layout output. Each Nepali name is paired with the English name at the same province and position, and the English name is matched to a COD-AB P-code (nepal-admin-districts 2.0.1) by name or alias within the same province; five English spellings are mapped by an explicit table: {"Makawanpur": "Makwanpur", "Nawalparasi (East of Bardaghat Susta)": "Nawalpur", "Rukun (Eastern Part)": "Rukum East", "Rukum (Western Part)": "Rukum West", "Daang": "Dang"}. Nothing is transliterated.
limitations: Names are as printed in Schedule 4, including its qualifiers (for example for the two Nawalparasi and the two Rukum districts).
The Nepali text layer was converted from the Preeti font; the conversion is letter for letter, and every name is checked to be clean Devanagari.
Schedule 4 numbers provinces 1 to 7; province names adopted later are not part of it.
uncertainty: None in the names themselves; a district renamed by a later amendment would need a new release.
